QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_4

question.text: Which of the following is PROHIBITED in issue advertisements under SEBI ICDR norms?

answer.text: Using the normal commercial name of the issuer company
Using celebrities or fictional characters to promote the issue
Disclosing risk factors alongside highlights of the issue
Mentioning brands that have already been disclosed in the offer document

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI ICDR norms state that issue advertisements shall not display models, celebrities, fictional characters, landmarks, caricatures, or the like. Normal commercial names of the issuer and brands already disclosed in the offer document are permitted exceptions to the prohibition. The Trap: Candidates often assume any brand reference is banned. The rule specifically prohibits the listed depictions (celebrities, fictional characters, landmarks, caricatures) while permitting normal commercial names and disclosed brands. Note: When clearing an issue advertisement, check first that no prohibited element (celebrity, fictional character, landmark, caricature) appears, then confirm any brand reference is the issuer's normal commercial name or a brand already disclosed in the offer document.
